titleZh: 显得紧张的；愤怒的；生气的

collocations: be filled with anger：充满了愤怒
words.definition: 生气；愤怒 vt. 使愤怒；激怒
words.etymology: v. c. 1200, “to irritate, annoy, provoke,” from Old Norse angra “to grieve, vex, distress; to be vexed at, take offense with”. Meaning “excite to wrath, make angry” is from late 14c. n. Mid-13c., “hostile attitude, ill will, surliness”.
words.mnemonic: ang-（=tight, painful：拉紧的；疼痛的）+ -er（名词 / 动词后缀）→

collocations: be angry with / at sb.：对某人很生气
words.definition: 生气的；愤怒的；（海或天空）狂风暴雨的，波涛汹涌
examples: Her behavior really made me angry.
words.mnemonic: anger（生气；愤怒）+ -y（形容词后缀）→生气的，愤怒的

examples: Officials reacted angrily to those charges.

collocations: an anxious look / face / expression：忧虑的目光/面容/表情
words.definition: 忧虑的；担心的；焦急的；渴望的
words.etymology: 1620s, “greatly troubled by uncertainties,” from Latin anxius “solicitous, uneasy, troubled in mind”, figuratively “to torment, cause distress” (from PIE root *angh- “tight, painfully constricted, painful”). Meaning “earnestly desirous” (as in anxious to please) is from 1742.
examples: Parents are naturally anxious for their children.
words.mnemonic: anx-（=ang-, g、x音变=troubled in mind, cause distress, earnestly

collocations: to ask/look/wait anxiously：忧虑地问/看/等待
examples: Residents are anxiously awaiting a decision.
words.mnemonic: anxious（忧虑的；焦虑的）+ -ly（副词后缀）→忧虑地；焦虑地

collocations: acute/intense/deep anxiety：非常/极度/深深的忧虑
examples: Some hospital patients experience high levels of anxiety.
words.mnemonic: anx-（=ang-：忧虑的；焦急的；渴望的）+ -iety（名词后缀，表状

collocations: songs full of teenage angst：充满青少年焦虑的歌曲
words.definition: （对形势、事态、生活的）忧虑；焦虑
words.etymology: 1944, from a specialized use in psychology of German Angst “neurotic fear, anxiety, guilt, remorse,” from *angh- “tight, painfully constricted, painful.”
words.mnemonic: ang-（=anxiety, fear：焦虑；担忧）+ -st（表状态）→焦虑、担心的
